scientific_question: After equal numbers of occupied island populations are lost, does the spatial leverage of the lost populations predict subsequent contraction among the populations that initially remained?

minimum_temporal_design.t0: baseline occupied-source state used to compute source leverage from lagged occurrence plus response-independent geometry only
minimum_temporal_design.t1: loss-event census used to identify which t0 occupied sources disappeared
minimum_temporal_design.t2: future census used once as the downstream contraction endpoint
minimum_temporal_design.reason: the source-loss event and the downstream contraction endpoint must occur in different transitions

source_loss_exposure.baseline_sources: S0 = occupied populations at t0 under the prospectively frozen occurrence rule
source_loss_exposure.lost_sources: L01 = S0 minus S1, where S1 is occupancy at t1
source_loss_exposure.kernel: K_is = prospectively frozen nonnegative source-access kernel based on response-independent geometry and an externally justified or response-independently frozen operator; it may not be tuned on t1 or t2 outcomes
source_loss_exposure.target_specific_baseline_pressure: P_i(S0) = sum over s in S0 of K_is
source_loss_exposure.target_specific_lost_access_fraction: E_i = sum over s in L01 of K_is / P_i(S0), defined only where P_i(S0) > 0
source_loss_exposure.event_level_lost_leverage: Q_loss = sum over s in L01 of A_s / sum over r in S0 of A_r, where A_s = sum over prospectively eligible geometry targets i of K_is

future_endpoint.analysis_population: sites/populations occupied at t1 that were not members of L01 and satisfy the frozen t2 survey/applicability rule
future_endpoint.binary_endpoint: 1 = occupied/use state at t1 but absent/non-use at t2; 0 = occupied/use at both t1 and t2
future_endpoint.claim_term: subsequent observed occupancy/use contraction unless a system-specific latent-occupancy endpoint is prospectively justified

R0: system/region/time structure fixed before t2 access
R2: ordinary Euclidean distance to surviving t1 sources
reference_ladder.primary_contrast: heldout predictive loss of C minus R2 for the t2 contraction endpoint

primary_prediction.statement: After nominal source count, number of lost populations, habitat/current state, generic network context and ordinary surviving-source distance are represented, adding E_i improves held-out prediction of which t1-surviving populations contract by t2.
primary_prediction.support_rule: prospectively frozen cluster-macro C-minus-R2 point estimate < 0 and cluster-bootstrap 95% upper bound < 0
primary_prediction.required_cluster_unit: independent archipelago, species, or predeclared species-by-archipelago event cluster appropriate to the admitted system

secondary_predictions.name: event_level_loss_leverage
secondary_predictions.statement: For transitions with equal nominal source-loss count, greater Q_loss is associated with greater subsequent contraction among t1 survivors.

secondary_predictions.name: high_vs_low_leverage_single_loss
secondary_predictions.statement: Among one-source-loss events, loss of a source above the prospectively frozen leverage split predicts greater subsequent contraction than loss below that split.

anti_selection: do not choose a candidate because a known source loss was followed by a known decline
do not inspect confirmatory t2 occupancy before the operator, endpoint, exposure, reference ladder and heldout design are frozen
do not tune the graph scale, kernel, leverage split or occupancy threshold on t2 outcomes
do not redefine L01 using t2
do not include t0-to-t1 lost-source sites in the t1-to-t2 endpoint denominator
do not claim causality, rescue, recolonization or demographic persistence from predictive support alone
do not reuse the v1_121 global mammal system as confirmation
candidate_selection_rule: metadata-first only: repeated-census structure, unit identity, geometry, survey design, temporal coverage and data accessibility may be inspected; focal response directions and candidate-specific decline stories may not be used for admission
